name: RoboCasa365: Scaling Robot Learning in Everyday Environments
description: RoboCasa365 is a large-scale simulation benchmark and demonstration dataset for training generally capable domestic robots in realistic everyday environments. Developed by UT Austin researchers, RoboCasa365 dramatically expands upon the original 2024 RoboCasa release, introducing 365 household tasks guided by large language models across more than 2,500 photorealistic kitchen scenes and 3,200 3D objects. The dataset provides over 2,200 hours of robot demonstration data—comprising 600+ hours of human teleoperated demonstrations and 1,600+ hours of automated demonstrations—accompanied by frame-level subtask annotations specifying atomic skills and stages to benchmark hierarchical policy learning.

size.notes: Demonstrations and asset packages are downloadable through python download_datasets.py scripts from Hugging Face and cloud mirrors.

provenance.collection_method: Simulated human VR teleoperation and automated trajectory synthesis in robosuite kitchen environments powered by RoboSuite v1.5.
provenance.curation_notes: Features 365 composite and atomic tasks. Builds upon the 2024 RSS release with subtask annotation labelers generating step-level instructions and stage markers directly from simulation states.
